ops.title: hermes-docker-proxy: screen bind/mount DESTINATION (block docker.sock relay)
ops.description:
Discovered + verified during the apple-container prototype (cc-notes log apple-container-prototype, 2026-07-15). `hermes-docker-proxy` screens bind/mount SOURCES against BindRoots but never DESTINATIONS (pkgs/hermes-docker-proxy/policy.go: mount struct has no Target field; the Binds loop ~187-195 and Mounts loop ~198-211 check source only).

**Impact under a socktainer migration (CRITICAL, verified live)**: socktainer transparently relays a container-internal `/var/run/docker.sock` TARGET to its own raw, unfiltered API regardless of the mount source. An agent behind the proxy did: `docker run -v <bindroot>/empty:/var/run/docker.sock` (passes screening) → inside, `/var/run/docker.sock` became a live socktainer socket → `docker run --privileged -v /:/hostroot` mounted the HOST filesystem (read `/Users/yasyf` = sops key + vault token). Full proxy bypass → host compromise.

**Current dockerd status**: NOT currently exploitable (dockerd has no docker.sock auto-relay), so this is a latent/defense-in-depth fix for the live proxy but a HARD PREREQUISITE for any socktainer/apple-container migration.

**Ready fix** (verified to close the bypass, existing tests green): add `forbiddenDest(dst)` rejecting any bind/mount whose destination basename is `docker.sock`; parse the Binds destination (after the first `:`) and the Mounts `Target`/`Destination`; call it in both loops. A working patch sits in `~/.yclaw/spike-container/proxy-patched/policy.go` on the host — port it into pkgs/hermes-docker-proxy/policy.go with a regression test that reproduces the bypass body and asserts the 403.

ops.text: screenCreate rejects any Binds/Mounts entry whose DESTINATION basename is docker.sock (both -v and --mount forms), with a unit test reproducing the socktainer docker.sock-relay bypass
A legitimate bind into a BindRoot with a normal destination still passes (no over-block); existing tests stay green
